Price structure

What keeps repeating on the chart?

Eight short chapters

01Price structure02Base & repricing03Supply zones04Demand & absorption05Holder rotation06Expansion & pullback07Continuation vs distribution08Swing lifecycle

01Definition

Structure is the sequence of highs, lows, ranges, and reactions built over time.

02Why it matters

Repeated reactions give you areas to investigate; one candle rarely tells the whole story.

03What to check

  • Several highs and lows on the same timeframe
  • Repeated reaction areas
  • Whether price holds or rejects a new range

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

Repeated tests and reactions support a clear working structure.

Dangerous

A single bounce or wick becomes the entire thesis.

05Beginner mistake

Drawing precise lines without checking the reactions behind them.

06Takeaway

Read repeated behavior before naming a pattern.

ILLUSTRATIVE · NOT A LIVE TOKEN

See the idea

  1. 01

    Price makes a high, pulls back, then makes a higher high.

  2. 02

    The next pullback holds above the earlier low.

  3. 03

    That supports rising structure; losing that low would weaken it.

Try it on a token

See it in Meme Fast → Swing

Find an exact token and review observed history. Use Inspect's 5D view or an external chart for detailed candle reactions.

Go deeper

Old entry areas can influence later selling, but a chart cannot identify trapped holders or their motives. Structure is observed price behavior; the ownership explanation needs separate evidence.
